title: Recombinase-mediated cassette exchange system for functional genomics in Mycoplasma mycoides
author: Noskov, Ma, et al.
materials: A 7.5 kilobase (kb) TAR cloning vector was generated by PCR amplification of pRC60 using two primers (5′- ACTAATAATAAAACATTTATATACTTAATGAATAAATATAATTAGTACCGTTCGTATAATGTATGC-3′ and 5′-ATTTTAAAATTTATGTAATTTATTAATTTTTATCTTTATAATATATACCGTTCGTATATGGTTTCT-3′) and the Phusion Hot Start High-Fidelity DNA polymerase with HF buffer (New England Biolabs; NEB) according to the manufacturer’s instructions with modifications. The reactions were supplemented with 1 mM additional MgCl2, and the products were annealed at 64°C and extended for 1 min per kb. Two 50-bp TAR cloning hooks (italicized) are homologous sequences necessary for recombination [13]. Approximately 40 ng of vector was co-transformed with 1 μg of sheared M. mycoides-syn1.0 genomic DNA [2] into VL6-48 spheroplasts. Transformants were selected on SD minus tryptophan.

The pRC59 vector was used as the DNA template for production of two landing pad cassettes (forward and reverse). A 3.4 kb of the forward landing pad cassette was PCR-amplified using Phusion Hot Start High-Fidelity DNA polymerase (New England Biolabs; NEB) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Primers (5′-AAATCAAGATCTTTTGGCAGCATATTTCTACTCTTTTTCTATTTATTAGT TACCGTTCGTATAAGAAACCA-3′ and 5′-TGATTACAACTAGTTTAACAATTTATTAAAAAACTTCGTAAAAACGAAGT TACCGTTCGTATAGCATACAT-3′) were used for production of the forward cassette and primers (5′-TAAGTTCTTATGATTACAACTAGTTTAACAATTTATTAAAAAACTTCGTAAAAACGAAGT TACCGTTCGTATAAGAAACCA-3′ and 5′-TTGTAGCTTAAAATCAAGATCTTTTGGCAGCATATTTCTACTCTTTTTCTATTTATTAGTTACCGTTCGTATAGCATACAT-3′) were used for production of the reverse cassette. Approximately 1 μg of PCR product was transformed into the yeast strain W303 containing the M. mycoides genome. Transformants were selected on SD minus leucine. All primers were purchased from Integrated DNA Technologies (Coralville, IA, USA).

Yeast colonies were patched to an appropriate selection medium and grown overnight at 30°C. Approximately 1 μl of cell mass was then picked up by pipette tip and twirled in a 0.5 ml PCR tube containing 10 μl of the zymolyase solution [10 μl of sterile water + 0.5 μl of 10 mg/ml of zymolyase 20T (ICN Biochemicals)]. The tube was incubated at 37°C for 1 hour, followed by 15 min incubation at 98°C. 1 μl of zymolyase-treated cells was analyzed by PCR using the QIAGEN Fast Cycling PCR Kit, according to the manufacturer's instructions.

The detailed preparation of genomic DNA in agarose plugs from yeast and M. mycoides cells was described previously [2,10]. Once prepared, yeast plugs were loaded onto a 1% Tris-acetate-EDTA agarose gel and electrophoresis was performed at 4.5 V per cm for 2 hours to remove yeast genomic DNA from the plugs (the circular M. mycoides genomes remained in the plug) [14]. To analyze the genomic structure by restriction digestion, half of an agarose plug was washed once with 1 ml of 0.1X Wash Buffer (Bio-Rad CHEF Genomic DNA Plug Kit) for 1 hour followed by 1 hour of washing with the same buffer plus 0.5 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (Sigma, St. Louis, MO). Plugs were then equilibrated with 1 ml of 1X Buffer 3 (NEB) for 1 hour. The genomic DNA was digested with 50 units of the restriction enzymes BssHII in 250 μl of 1X buffer 3 for 5 hours at 37°C. Following incubation, plugs were subjected to pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (CHEF DRIII, Bio-Rad). Pulse times were ramped from 20 to 50 seconds for 16 hours at 6.0 V/cm. All restriction enzymes were purchased from NEB.

We previously reported the synthesis of the 1,078 kb M. mycoides-syn1.0 genome, followed by genome transplantation to produce the first synthetic cell [2]. The construction of the synthetic genome was performed in three hierarchical stages by transformation and homologous recombination in yeast, starting with assembling 10 kb, to 100 kb, to the complete 1,078 kb genome. To verify the functionality of the synthetic 100 kb intermediates, semi-synthetic genomes were assembled from a synthetic piece and 10 native ones, followed by transplantation analysis [2]. While this approach enabled us to build a variety of genomes for testing, the efficiency of complete assembly was very low (~2 to 5%). Furthermore, the procedure of genome assembly was tedious and time-consuming since it involved isolation of large pieces of DNA from yeast and purification of DNA fragments by electrophoresis [14]. By using the swapping system described above, we showed that the semi-synthetic genome could be easily constructed (50% efficiency) and that the effort and time were significantly reduced. In addition, we found that cloning or assembly of an insert DNA to the donor vector could be conducted directly in a yeast strain harboring the M. mycoides genome with the insertion of the landing pad where the cassette exchange could be performed. This further simplifies the procedure of genome construction without the steps of the donor DNA preparation and transformation (unpublished result). We also demonstrated that this swapping system can facilitate the study of genome organization by inverting the same synthetic piece in the opposite orientation. Previous studies of genome rearrangements were conducted by creation of inversion through insertion of two loxP sites flanking the target region of interest where the Cre recombinase triggered the rearrangement [16], and a similar approach using the Frt/Flp recombinase was also reported [17]. However, these approaches only allow a one-time inversion event.

steps.title: Grow yeast strains
steps.instruction: Cultivate S. cerevisiae strains VL6‑48 and W303‑1a (both containing the 1.08‑Mb M. mycoides genome) in YEPD (glucose) or YEPG (galactose) rich medium, or in synthetic minimal dextrose medium (SD), at 30 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Transform yeast with RMCE plasmids
steps.instruction: Introduce plasmid pRC59 (landing‑pad cassette) and plasmid pRC60 (donor cassette) into the chosen yeast strain using either the lithium‑acetate method or the spheroplast method, and select transformants on SD‑His (for pRC59) and SD‑Trp (for pRC60) plates.

steps.title: Induce Cre‑mediated cassette exchange
steps.instruction: Grow co‑transformants in SD‑Gal medium (galactose as carbon source) for 24 h at 30 °C to induce Cre recombinase expression from the GAL1 promoter.

steps.title: Select uracil prototrophs and PCR‑screen
steps.instruction: Plate the galactose‑induced culture on SD‑Uracil plates; pick individual colonies and perform PCR with primers swap‑F and swap‑R. A 1.1 kb product indicates successful pRC59S exchange, whereas a 3.6 kb product indicates the parental pRC59.

steps.title: Amplify TAR cloning vector
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify pRC60 using the following primers (5′‑ACTAATAATAAAACATTTATATACTTAATGAATAAATATAATTAGTACCGTTCGTATAATGTATGC‑3′ and 5′‑ATTTTAAAATTTATGTAATTTATTAATTTTTATCTTTATAATATATACCGTTCGTATATGGTTTCT‑3′) with Phusion Hot‑Start High‑Fidelity DNA polymerase (NEB) in HF buffer, adding 1 mM MgCl₂, annealing at 64 °C, and extending 1 min per kb to generate a 7.5 kb TAR vector.

steps.title: Perform TAR cloning of 100 kb segment
steps.instruction: Co‑transform approximately 40 ng of the 7.5 kb TAR vector with 1 µg of sheared M. mycoides‑syn1.0 genomic DNA into VL6‑48 spheroplasts; select transformants on SD‑Trp plates. The TAR hooks (two 50‑bp homologous sequences) facilitate recombination of the 100 kb target segment into the vector.

steps.title: Amplify and insert landing‑pad cassette
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify the 3.4 kb forward landing‑pad cassette using Phusion polymerase and primers 5′‑AAATCAAGATCTTTTGGCAGCATATTTCTACTCTTTTTCTATTTATTAGTTACCGTTCGTATAAGAAACCA‑3′ and 5′‑TGATTACAACTAGTTTAACAATTTATTAAAAAACTTCGTAAAAACGAAGTTACCGTTCGTATAGCATACAT‑3′; similarly amplify the reverse cassette with primers 5′‑TAAGTTCTTATGATTACAACTAGTTTAACAATTTATTAAAAAACTTCGTAAAAACGAAGTTACCGTTCGTATAAGAAACCA‑3′ and 5′‑TTGTAGCTTAAAATCAAGATCTTTTGGCAGCATATTTCTACTCTTTTTCTATTTATTAGTTACCGTTCGTATAGCATACAT‑3′. Transform ~1 µg of each PCR product into yeast strain W303 containing the M. mycoides genome, and select on SD‑Leu plates.

steps.title: Screen colonies by colony PCR
steps.instruction: Patch each colony onto appropriate selection medium and incubate overnight at 30 °C. Pick ~1 µl of cell mass with a pipette tip, vortex in a 0.5 ml PCR tube containing 10 µl zymolyase solution (9.5 µl sterile water + 0.5 µl of 10 mg/ml Zymolyase 20T). Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h, then heat‑inactivate at 98 °C for 15 min. Use 1 µl of this lysate as template for PCR with the QIAGEN Fast Cycling PCR Kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Prepare plugs and run restriction analysis
steps.instruction: Prepare agarose plugs containing genomic DNA from yeast or M. mycoides cells as described previously. Load plugs onto a 1 % Tris‑acetate‑EDTA agarose gel and electrophorese at 4.5 V cm⁻¹ for 2 h to remove yeast chromosomal DNA. Wash half of each plug once with 1 ml 0.1 X Wash Buffer (Bio‑Rad CHEF Genomic DNA Plug Kit) for 1 h, then wash for another hour with the same buffer containing 0.5 mM PMSF. Equilibrate plugs in 1 ml 1 X Buffer 3 (NEB) for 1 h. Digest with 50 U BssHII in 250 µl 1 X Buffer 3 at 37 °C for 5 h. Separate digested DNA by pulsed‑field gel electrophoresis on a CHEF‑DRIII system (Bio‑Rad) with pulse times ramped from 20 to 50 s for 16 h at 6.0 V cm⁻¹. Visualize bands to confirm expected fragment sizes (e.g., 668 kb + 317 kb for landing‑pad insertion; 668 kb + 224 kb + 193 kb for semi‑synthetic genome).

steps.title: Induce cassette exchange for semi‑synthetic genome
steps.instruction: Transform the donor plasmid pRC60 (carrying the 100 kb synthetic segment cloned by TAR) into the yeast strain that already harbors the landing‑pad‑replaced genome (step 7). Grow transformants in SD‑Gal medium for 24 h to induce Cre recombinase, then plate on SD‑Uracil plates. Verify exchange at both junctions by PCR with appropriate primers; expect >50 % correct exchange. Confirm genome structure by the BssHII restriction analysis described in step 9.

steps.title: Construct inverted semi‑synthetic genome (optional)
steps.instruction: Re‑insert the landing‑pad cassette in the opposite orientation by homologous recombination, transform the same pRC60 donor plasmid, induce Cre with galactose for 24 h, select on SD‑Uracil, and screen by PCR (≈50 % correct). Verify inversion by BssHII digestion, which should yield 668 kb, 212 kb and 204 kb fragments.
